findings.description: AWS access key ID and secret access key are committed in plain text as Lambda environment variables. Anyone with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration or read access to the repository can retrieve these long-lived static credentials, and they persist in version control history even if removed.

No kms_key_arn is set, so the environment variables (which hold secrets here) are encrypted only with the default service-owned AWS key. A customer-managed CMK would allow explicit key policy, rotation and revocation control over who can decrypt the function configuration.
The function pins runtime nodejs12.x, which is past end of life and no longer receives security patches from AWS, leaving known vulnerabilities in the execution environment unfixed.

No code_signing_config_arn is configured, so the deployment package uploaded from resources/lambda_function_payload.zip is not signature-verified before execution; tampering with the artefact between build and deployment would be undetectable.

findings.issue_category: missing permissions boundary and confused-deputy guard
findings.description: The Lambda execution role's trust policy allows lambda.amazonaws.com to assume it with no aws:SourceAccount or aws:SourceArn condition and no permissions boundary attached, so nothing constrains the maximum privilege that can later be delegated to this role or scopes trust to this account's functions.
